sentences.text: In the crossexamination of Pws.1and 2 nothing worth is elicited to disbelieve the alleged manner of accident.

The counsel for respondent No.2 contends that there is a delay in lodging the first information and the  12 MVC No.1517 &1518/2021  SCCH-25 IMV report clearly shows there was negligence on the part of the rider of the bike itself.

The Pws.1 and 2 clearly deposed that as the owner of the Car assured them that he will pay the treatment expenses and hence the delay is caused in lodging the first information, the said fact is not disproved by the respondent No.2 by leading evidence

and moreover in view of decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan it is settled law that mere delay in lodging the first information is not fatal to claim compensation by the victims and hence as the delay is satisfactorily explained and in the absence of any contrary evidence by the insurance company the delay offered is acceptable.

Though pointing out the damages mentioned in Ex.P.3 the counsel for insurance company contends that there was negligence on the part of the petitioner/rider of the bike but as per the police documents the driver of the car suddenly took the car towards left side which lead to accident and to prove the  13 MVC No.1517 &1518/2021  SCCH-25 contrary to this the respondent No.2 has not lead any evidence of either eye witness or the driver of the Car and Mr.K.N.Nanjappa vs In Both The Cases:

13. Further, the documents produced by the petitioners i.e., the FIR, FIS, Statement in Cr.No.107/2020, mahazar, seizure mahazar, MVA report and charge sheet as per Exs.P.1 to P.3, P.5, P.14 and P.15 are the public documents issued by a public office and they have got presumptive value under law.
The Respondent No.2 have not obtained any contrary admissions from the mouth of the PWs.1 and 2 to support their defence.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 and documents produced by them and accept the version of the Respondent No.2.

Further, the wound certificates produced by the Petitioners  14 MVC No.1517 &1518/2021  SCCH-25 as per Exs.P.4 and P.9 clearly disclose that, on account of accident the Petitioners have sustained simple and grievous injuries.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The Petitioners have filed these petitions under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicle Act seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by them in a road accident dated  3 MVC No.1517 &1518/2021  SCCH-25 24.11.2020.
Due to impact, petitioners fell down along with the bike and sustained grievous injuries.
Prior to the date of  7 MVC No.1517 &1518/2021  SCCH-25 accident he was hale and healthy and was earning his livelihood as two wheeler Mechanic, earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month and on account of said accidental injuries till today he cannot attend to his work, resulted in loss of earnings, earning capacity and put to great financial hardship.
 5. Further it is case of the petitioners that, the Hirisave Police have registered a case in their Cr.No.107/2020, after investigation the said police have filed charge sheet against the said Driver, punishable under Sec.279 & 338 of IPC.
7. The Respondent No.1 in the written statement has denied the averments of the petitions as false,
admitted issuance of policy but subject to its terms and conditions and submitted that there is noncompliance of Sections 134(c), 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, the insured vehicle was said to be driven by a person not possession valid and effective driving license and first respondent knowingly and willfully entrusted his vehicle to such a person at that time of accident, hence there is a express breach of Driver's clauses absolving the insurer from any liability.
There is a delay in lodging the first information.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petitions against them.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the Petitioners prove that,
 the accident occurred due to rash and  negligent driving by the Driver of Car  bearing Reg.No.KA13M4640 and in  the said accident they have sustained  injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioners prove that  they are entitled to the compensation  amount claimed ?
If so from whom  and to what extent ?
3. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The counsel for respondent No.2 contends that there is a delay in lodging the first information and the  12 MVC No.1517 &1518/2021  SCCH-25 IMV report clearly shows there was negligence on the part of the rider of the bike itself.
The Pws.1 and 2 clearly deposed that as the owner of the Car assured them that he will pay the treatment expenses and hence the delay is caused in lodging the first information, the said fact is not disproved by the respondent No.2 by leading evidence
and moreover in view of decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan it is settled law that mere delay in lodging the first information is not fatal to claim compensation by the victims and hence as the delay is satisfactorily explained and in the absence of any contrary evidence by the insurance company the delay offered is acceptable.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Respondent No.2 have not obtained any contrary admissions from the mouth of the PWs.1 and 2 to support their defence.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 and documents produced by them and accept the version of the Respondent No.2.
Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PWs.1 and 2 coupled with documents produced by them, this court is of the opinion that, the driver of the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA13 M4640 driven the same in a rash and negligent manner,
so as to endangering to human life with a high speed and overtook the motorcycle and suddenly took left turn Mr.K.N.Nanjappa vs In Both The Cases: 1. Venkatesha M.S on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127205889/
10 towards service road from the extreme right side without showing indicator or and signal and dashed to the motorcycle in which the petitioners were going and caused the accident, result of which the Petitioners have sustained simple and grievous injuries.
He also has not placed any disability certificate issued by the competent authority/doctor and also not lead any Mr.K.N.Nanjappa vs In Both The Cases: 1.
Therefore, the version of the Petitioner that the injuries sustained in the accident have  16 MVC No.1517 &1518/2021  SCCH-25 caused him permanent disability resulting loss of income is not acceptable and under these circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.45,000/ under the heads of Pain and Suffering.
Therefore, the version of the Petitioner that he was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ per month is not acceptable but the notional income needs to be considered.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 44 years as could be make out from Ex.P.11/Aadhar card of the petitioner.
The accident took place in the year 2020.
Therefore, the respondents being the insurer and the RC owner are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, as the policy is existed and hence the respondent No.2 insurer is directed to indemnify the respondent No.1/owner and to deposit the compensation.
